scenes.text: Day two hundred twelve. You're the only one awake on the cargo ship Meridian.
Five crew. Four of them frozen in cryosleep. Your job is simple. Stay awake. Watch the ship. Wake no one.
For seven months, nothing has happened. No signals. No ships. The nearest human being is four hundred million miles away.
Then, at three in the morning, the proximity alarm goes off. Something is touching the hull.
It isn't debris. It isn't drifting. It's crawling along the outside of the ship, straight toward the airlock.
Three slow knocks. From the outside. Nothing out there should be alive.
You wipe the frost from the glass. A figure in a spacesuit. It lifts one hand, and presses it against the window.
Then you read the name tag. R. Voss. Pilot. That is your name.
But your suit is hanging in the locker behind you. Exactly where you left it.
Then the radio crackles. And your own voice says: Please. Let me in. I'm the real one.

choice.narration: Do you open the airlock? Or keep it sealed?
choice.question: WHAT DO YOU DO?
